transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Elliot Park (Atlas Head of ML), Maya Singh (Atlas Platform), Jon Rivera (Atlas Security), Lina Wu (Atlas PM)

Summary:
Quick migration/demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API, plus overview of Console and Optimize features. Discussed streaming, function calling parity, embedding differences, VPC/private deployment options, SOC2/KMS, and next steps for a POC and benchmarks.

Topics:
- API parity (endpoints, params, streaming, function call mapping)
- Embeddings differences and batching/throughput
- Console + Optimize for cost/perf tuning
- Private/VPC and security/compliance items
- POC logistics and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll kick off, hi elliot, maya, jon, lina, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Elliot (Atlas): yeah loud and clear, thanks for setting this up aisha.
[00:08] Marco (Redwood SE): hi all, i'm marco, i'll run through the parity demo part - map the openai/anthropic/together calls to redwood api, show the console and optimize bits.
[00:15] Maya (Atlas): quick note, we're currently using OpenAI for chat + embeddings, and Together for some local LLM experiments. latency is... uh our SLO is ~200ms tail for short assists, embeddings are batched. security wise, jon will ask about k m s and audit logs.
[00:30] Jon (Atlas Security): yes we need SOC2 docs, KMS integration, and also an audit log we can ship to our splunk, and VPC peering options.
[00:38] Aisha: absolutely, we'll share the security pack. marco - can you start on the API mapping?
[00:42] [00:42] Marco: sure. so first, the high-level: Redwood exposes a single REST endpoint for text generation and chat, plus an embeddings endpoint. for chat parity with OpenAI chat completions, you send messages array, role tokens, same idea. function calling is supported - we have the same pattern for function schema, but note: function call name mapping is preserved and we stream JSON chunks in the same manner. small caveat - the default streaming chunking can differ by chunk size, but you can tune chunk window in request params.
[01:12] Maya: when you say messages array, is there any different token accounting? we saw some token delta when switching providers before.
[01:18] Marco: good q. token accounting is model dependent - when you pick a redwood-verified model we provide a token profile in the console. we also provide a tokenizer endpoint (or token info in the SDK) so you can pre-tokenize. in practice we've seen 2-6% variation vs OpenAI depending on model/tokenizer, so we report effective tokens and cost per token in the dashboard.
[01:36] Elliot: ok, and embeddings - Together uses a different vector dim for their models sometimes, how do we map?
[01:41] Marco: embeddings map is straightforward: we give model mapping table, e.g. together-embedding-xx maps to redwood-embed-small (1536) or redwood-embed-large (3072). we also support on-the-fly dimension conversion for similarity lookup - we ship a small converter in the SDK, but best practice is to pick the same dimensionality to avoid reindexing.
[01:58] [02:00] Aisha: i'll drop the mapping doc after this call - it will include exact endpoint examples, curl/snippets for openai->redwood, anthropic->redwood, together->redwood.
[02:08] Lina (Atlas): nice. can you demo the console route mapping and rollout controls? we want canary behavior for critical flows.
[02:15] Marco: yes. switching to screen share - (screen share noise) - okay seeing the console, first panel is routes, you can pin a route to a model variant, set rollback policies and canary percentages, and set tiering by latency/cost. an interesting bit is automatic fallback: if your primary model is out of capacity, we can route to a quantized variant or different region automatically.
[02:44] Maya: does console show per-token cost? we need to compare cost on the same workload.
[02:49] Marco: yes per-route cost and token breakdown, and you can export to CSV. plus Optimize suggests batching and quantization based on real traces.
[02:58] [03:05] Elliot: curious about latency. our peak qps for small prompts is ~120 rps, tail p95 is what we care about. how are you measuring and guaranteeing?
[03:12] Marco: for hosted we have latency SLOs and dedicated tiers for predictability. for the POC we recommend Dedicated or Private to get stable p95. the runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache optimization, which reduces token compute time for chat with long histories.
[03:28] Jon: about private deployment - we need a VPC option or on-prem package. is HSM KMS available?
[03:34] Marco: yes VPC + private control plane is supported. KMS/HSM integration is available in Private deployments - we have docs listing supported providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault), and we can produce network diagrams for your security review.
[03:48] [04:00] Aisha: jon i'll make sure the security pack arrives. any other compliance must-haves?
[04:06] Jon: data residency - some PII flows must stay in eu-region. can you pin region?
[04:11] Marco: yes region pinning and data residency is possible with private deployments and dedicated region commitments. for hosted, you can select region endpoints, but for strict residency we recommend Private.
[04:21] Maya: how hard is the migration code-level? do we have example SDK calls?
[04:26] Marco: yes, we have language SDKs and a compatibility shim. example - OpenAI chat.create -> Redwood chat.completions with same messages payload. i will share a small shim that rewrites auth header and endpoints, minimal code changes. for streaming we support the same SSE-style pattern and also an optional websocket.
[04:46] [05:00] Elliot: any gotchas with function calling? we use function calling heavily for agent orchestration.
[05:05] Marco: function calling behaves similarly; one difference to note - Redwood returns function call chunks in an assembly stream and you can request full assembled JSON or incremental partials. some SDKs default to assemble; others give you raw chunks - easy toggle. Also, schema validation is slightly stricter by default (to reduce mismatch).
[05:30] Aisha: can you show Optimize recommendations?
[05:34] Marco: switching to the Optimize tab - here we ingest traces (or you can upload a trace file), we recommend batching window, quantization profile per model, and suggest a candidate model map for cost/perf. e.g. for your short-assist workload it suggests redwood-2-small-8bit with 8-bit quantization and aggressive batching to hit cost targets while preserving p95.
[06:02] Maya: about quantization - we're worried about quality regression. do you have quality monitoring?
[06:07] Marco: yes Quality Monitor ties to prompt sets and evals. we run canary evals and regression alerts. if a quantized model drifts, Optimize can auto-roll back or notify and open a ticket.
[06:20] Elliot: good. one more thing - embeddings recall for semantic search, we use Milvus/FAISS. how to avoid reindexing if dims change?
[06:27] Marco: two options: dimension converter helper (approx) or reindex. we generally recommend picking consistent embed dim; Optimize can show tradeoffs (cost vs recall) and recommend which model to pick to minimize reindex work.
[06:40] [07:00] Lina: let's talk POC shape - we want a perf benchmark (latency/p95/p99), embedding accuracy eval, and a 2-week pilot on a dedicated capacity.
[07:09] Aisha: sounds good. marco, can you own the perf harness and test plan?
[07:13] Marco: yes i'll build a harness; will need atlas sample prompts and data, and an expected SLA. recommended test: 2k requests, mixed prompt lengths, 4k context for some, embedding batch sizes up to 256.
[07:27] Maya: we can provide prompts and a small eval set and our retriever hits baseline.
[07:31] Elliot: timeline - we'd like results in 2 weeks if possible.
[07:34] Marco: doable if we get data and access.
[07:37] [08:00] Jon: security specifics - can you push audit logs to our SIEM? and what's retention?
[08:06] Aisha: yes logs via syslog/S3 push, retention can be configured at the tenant level; enterprise plans include longer retention. i'll include exact retention options in the security pack.
[08:16] Jon: also need an escalation contact for incidents.
[08:19] Aisha: we'll provide on-call chart and SLA contact for the pilot.
[08:25] [09:00] Maya: pricing - rough ballpark for dedicated capacity?
[09:03] Aisha: i'll send tiers; roughly there's a committed monthly for dedicated GPUs + per-token adjustments for heavy bursts. for pilots we can do a short-term reserved with burst credits.
[09:14] Elliot: do you support preemptible instances for cheaper compute?
[09:17] Marco: we support burst capacity and lower-cost quantized variants, but for strict availability we don't recommend preemptible for core latency-sensitive flows. Could use as a fallback tier for non-critical batch jobs.
[09:31] [10:00] Lina: question on tool calling and structured outputs - can we force outputs to match JSON schema?
[10:05] Marco: yes we have structured output helpers and a schema enforcement layer; you can request strict schema validation and get clear failure vs auto-repair heuristics.
[10:15] Aisha: any immediate blockers from atlas side?
[10:18] Elliot: main blockers: Jon's security review, and getting sample prompts/data for the perf harness.
[10:24] Aisha: okay i'll follow up with the security pack and mapping doc. marco will pick up tech.
[10:28] [11:00] (brief cross-talk; small audio glitch)
[11:20] Marco: quick note on monitoring - we expose per-request traces, token heatmaps, and a model-level regression dashboard. you can create alerts on drift or token spend.
[11:32] Maya: can you annotate cost per-route by customer team? we want chargeback.
[11:36] Marco: yes per-route tags and cost allocation is in the console, plus export for billing.
[11:42] [12:00] Jon: one more - network egress concerns for embeddings, can you do private connectivity?
[12:07] Marco: yes VPC peering/direct connect supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we provide TLS+region restrictions but not direct connect.
[12:15] Lina: awesome.
[12:18] [13:00] Aisha: recap and next steps: i'll send mapping doc + pricing + security pack by tuesday 5/18; marco will schedule a 2-hour POC bench week of 5/25 and will prepare harness; atlas to share prompts/data by 5/20; jon to send compliance Qs by 5/19.
[13:40] Elliot: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[13:44] Maya: thanks, bye.
[13:46] Marco: thanks all, bye.
